thread:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: P1 alert — sustained spike of 502/504 responses from api-gateway-edge (us-west-2). paging on-call. alert window started ~2950012300.
oncall-bot: Incident channel opened automatically: #incidents — thread created. Paging: @alex (on-call), @jamie (sre), @priya (edge), @sam (platform).
alex: on it. seeing the page. quick ask — customer impact? logs or dashboards?
jamie: dashboards show 502 rate jumped from ~0.4% -> 18% over last 6m for /v1/generate and /v1/chat endpoints on edge nodes in us-west-2. overall traffic same. error bursts aligned with higher tail latencies.
priya: I'm pulling edge-proxy logs now. early signs: upstreams returning 502 and 504, looks like model-router instances are timing out behind the gateway. snippet: ```[edge-proxy] 2026-03-15T12:07:14Z upstream connect error: read timeout from 10.12.7.88: upstream status=504```
jamie: deploy-bot shows a recent edge proxy config push at 2950011200 by @jamie — nothing suspicious in the diff. also no recent autoscaler changes.
deploy-bot: Deploy 2950011200: edge-proxy config pushed by jamie. Commit d9f2b4. No rollback detected.
sam: can we confirm whether model-router pods in us-west-2 are overloaded or if it's a networking/connectivity issue to the runtime? I can scale model-router if needed.
priya: `kubectl get pods -n runtime -l app=model-router -o wide` shows many pods in CrashLoopBackoff and some with `OOMKilled` and several at high CPU. e.g. `model-router-7f6b8` restarts 3x in last 5m.
alex: OOMs — maybe a recent model variant is eating memory. Any correlation with customer traffic patterns?
jamie: Checking traffic by client_id: a handful of high-QPS API keys spiking. One client spiked 6x their usual. Could be a noisy tenant hitting heavy streaming requests.
priya: Running `kubectl logs model-router-7f6b8 -n runtime --tail 200` — seeing repeated `out of memory` GC and then grpc connection resets to edge. snippet: ```runtime error: cannot allocate memory; failing request generation -> send upstream 502```
alex: mitigation options: 1) scale model-router replicas now, 2) shift a portion of edge traffic to us-east-1 region, 3) enable per-key circuit breaker / rate limit for noisy keys, 4) temporarily fallback to a smaller model variant for heavy routes. Let's pick immediate safe ones: scale and traffic-shift.
sam: scaling now: `kubectl scale deploy/model-router --replicas=12 -n runtime` — scaled from 4 -> 12.
sam: also bumping node pool autoscaler in us-west-2 — requesting extra capacity.
jamie: I'll prepare a traffic shift runbook step. We can move 50% of new edge traffic to us-east-1 via the regional-router.
priya: before shifting, we should add a 10s upstream timeout to edge-proxy to reduce queuing and free sockets. Applying quick config now.
priya: Done. edge-proxy timeout set to 10s.
priya: After timeout change, immediate drop in queuing observed on the edge nodes, but error rate still high ~12%.
alex: start traffic shift 40% -> us-east-1 to reduce pressure in us-west-2. Use routing tool.
jamie: running `regional-router shift --from us-west-2 --to us-east-1 --percent 40 --dry-run=false`
jamie: SHIFT command executed. Traffic move in progress — expect propagation ~30s.
edge-monitor-bot: Traffic distribution updated: us-west-2 60% | us-east-1 40%. Health checks OK for us-east-1.
priya: seeing 502s drop on the shifted gateway fleet. us-west-2 still 6-8% while scale/autoscale catches up.
jamie: any customer-facing impact? support metrics?
alex: support -> notify SRE/Sales for top affected customers. I see increased 5xx for two enterprise customers — opening a quick SR draft.
priya: for a more durable mitigation, we should enable per-key throttles for the noisy API keys. I can add a 1k req/min cap for the top offenders.
sam: added temporary rate limits for three client_ids. Confirmed via policy service.
alex: good. also enable fallback model variant for heavy streaming endpoints to reduce memory pressure. Priya, can you flip fallback policy?
priya: flipping fallback to light-quantized variant for `/v1/generate` for the noisy routes. Policy toggle done.
jamie: monitoring — overall 5xx across the full fleet down to 1.6% in last 2m, median latency back to normal.
edge-monitor-bot: Aggregated metrics: 5xx(t=1m)=1.5%, tail latency p95=380ms, request rate stable.
alex: great. keep monitoring. I'll mark incident as "mitigated" in the tracker once numbers stable for 15m.
priya: root cause hypothesis: model-router memory pressure caused by a combo of (a) sudden noisy tenant traffic pattern, (b) a recently onboarded model variant with higher memory footprint, and (c) insufficient immediate autoscaling headroom.
jamie: next actions (short): 1) increase model-router max replicas and pods memory request caps, 2) add per-tenant circuit breaker defaults, 3) add early detection alert when pod OOMs > 2 within 10m.
alex: assign owners — sam for autoscale and pod sizing, priya for circuit breaker + fallback policy, jamie for alert tuning and runbook updates.
sam: I'll follow up with infra to expedite node pool scale and raise default cluster node limit.
priya: I'll draft a quick post-incident runbook snippet for noisy tenants and fallback toggles.
jamie: I'll tune alerts and add a synthetic that simulates high-QPS streaming to catch similar regressions.
alex: thanks all. I'll send a short customer-facing blurb for support to send to affected customers.
edge-monitor-bot: 15m monitor window — 5xx staying <2% for 10m. Marking incident: mitigated -> monitoring.
alex: (reacts :thumbsup:) leaving this thread open for postmortem notes. we'll reconvene for a full write-up tomorrow.
priya: copying key logs to the incident archive and tagging recent commits to review the model onboarding checklist.
jamie: ETA for full postmortem tomorrow EOD.
sam: noted, I'll have autoscale follow-up by EOD as well.
alex: closing notes: mitigation steps executed: scaled model-router, increased node pool, added upstream timeout, shifted 40% traffic regionally, added per-tenant rate limits, enabled fallback model variant. Long-term actions assigned. Good work. :white_check_mark:
